identity.title: Position: Current Model Licensing Practices are Dragging Us into a Quagmire of Legal Noncompliance

problem.claim: The paper examines whether current model-licensing practices create undesirable legal consequences amid widespread model reuse and publication.

gap.claim: No standard or widely accepted best practices currently guide model licensing.

contributions.claim: Argues that current model-licensing practices are leading toward widespread legal noncompliance.
Reviews widely adopted license clauses, compares model licenses, and identifies potential legal risks, illustrated with examples from real-world Hugging Face repositories.
Proposes draft ModelGo Licenses (MGLs) intended to support more standardized licensing and better compliance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce ModelGo Licenses as a proposed draft model-license family addressing the challenges they identify.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that clause review supports their position that current licensing practices are producing a legal-compliance quagmire.
The authors report demonstrating potential legal risks through examples drawn from real-world Hugging Face repositories.

narrative_sequence.summary: ML models are widely published and model-component reuse is prevalent.
Developers must choose licenses from several commonly used options, but shared best practices are absent.
The authors answer that missing standardization has undesirable consequences, reviewing licenses and identifying potential legal risks with repository examples.
They propose ModelGo Licenses to encourage standardization and better compliance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a broad position to clause review, license comparisons, identified risks, and concrete repository examples.

lessons.interpretation: A position paper can make an abstract-level case more inspectable by connecting normative claims to document analysis and grounded examples.
lessons.application: For a policy or governance argument, map each central concern to the relevant rule text and at least one concrete artifact or case.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when examples cannot be verified, are unrepresentative, or the claim requires systematic prevalence estimates.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify which license clauses or legal jurisdictions underpin the identified risks.
The number, selection, and details of Hugging Face repository examples are not reported.
No evaluation or adoption evidence for the proposed MGLs is provided.
